candidates.original_title: Do female and ethnically diverse executives endure inequity in the CEO position or do they benefit from their minority status? An empirical examination
candidates.description: Women CEOs receive higher compensation than male CEOs
candidates.citation_sentence: Our replication study, both with the original sample and the expanded sample, provides a contrast to HUB's findings, suggesting that claims about gender gap in CEO compensation favoring women over men may be premature.

candidates.original_title: Do female and ethnically diverse executives endure inequity in the CEO position or do they benefit from their minority status? An empirical examination
candidates.description: Female CEOs receive higher compensation than male CEOs because their minority status makes them a rare and valuable resource for their firms.
candidates.citation_sentence: Revisiting the gender gap in CEO compensation: Replication and extension of Hill, Upadhyay, and Beekun's (2015) work on CEO gender pay gap
candidates.notes: The paper reexamines the original 1996–2005 sample and extends the analysis to post-2005 and combined 1996–2014 samples, but all analyses concern the same female-CEO compensation effect. The authors explicitly state that the replication fails to find reliable evidence supporting the original female compensation premium.
